title: CBIC Clarifies GST Exemptions for R&D, Shipping, Bank Interest & NBFC Services (Circular No. 266/12/2026-GST)
content:
# CBIC Clarifies GST Exemptions for R&D, Shipping, Bank Interest & NBFC Services (Circular No. 266/12/2026-GST)

Ek important update hai! Government ne services par GST applicability ko lekar kuch significant clarifications announce kiye hain through Circular No. 266/12/2026-GST dated October 28, 2026, based on the recommendations of the 57th GST Council meeting.

Here are the key takeaways:

*   **R&D Services:** For research and development services supplied against grants by eligible institutions (Government Entities or notified research associations/universities/colleges under Section 35(1) of the Income Tax Act, 1961), a self-certification mechanism will be accepted. A certificate from the head of the institution confirming that the activity is R&D and not consultancy may suffice for claiming exemption under Entry 44A of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate).
*   **Shipping Services (Imports by Foreign Shipping Companies):** Services imported without consideration by an Indian establishment of a foreign shipping company from a related person or an overseas establishment are exempt from GST, effective November 1, 2026, via Notification No. 07/2026-Integrated Tax (Rate). For the period from July 1, 2017, to October 31, 2026, these past transactions have been regularized on an "as is where is" basis.
*   **Bank Interest (Fund Transfer Pricing):** Notional amounts or interest recorded by banks for loans or advances under their internal Fund Transfer Pricing (FTP) mechanism will be treated as 'interest' and thus remain exempt from GST under Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate).
*   **NBFC Services (Co-lending):** Services provided by Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) to banks under co-lending arrangements, including sourcing, appraisal, servicing, and recovery, are taxable under GST. The value of these services will be determined by the contractual agreement between the NBFC and the bank.
